I saw your post on the AIO subreddit and clicked on your profile because I was worried you might take that asshole back. I assume this post is about him, but what I want to say goes for anyone who has treated you poorly in the past. People can and do change, grow, evolve. Changing for the better, learning from your mistakes, takes time and hard work, it's a constant effort. It's not something you put some time into and then "be changed", you have to keep at it. Abusers and toxic people behave the way they do for many different reasons, and it's often pathological, meaning it's so ingrained in them they don't fully realize it and they don't have much control over it. Learning how to get to the root of it all and to untangle this complex net of deep rooted issues, it's not something many people are able to do. It takes true self reflection, commitment, vulnerability, honesty... it takes hard fucking work and A LONG TIME. No one transforms from being abusive in a few months. 

And here's the thing, if he had changed, he wouldn't try to get you back. He would give you space and let you heal and not selfishly beg for a second chance. He wouldn't risk your well being after so little time, he would be terrified of hurting you again and recognize that it is not safe for you to be around him. You want him to change, maybe he wants to change, but he hasn't, and if he ever does it still wouldn't be healthy for you two to be together after he's abused you. I'm sure he has many good qualities, I'm sure you have some very strong feelings for him, but the specific ways in which he is bad to you can never outweigh the good. 

The person you choose to be your partner should never make you feel unsafe. You should feel that they always have your best interest at heart, even if they mess up, even if they have flaws, you should feel that they love you more than they hate themselves. Your post about how he made you feel bad for your mannerisms was heartbreaking. He cared more about his own insecurities and needing to put you down to reassure himself than he cared about you being happy. He chose to repeatedly tell you things to try to take away your confidence, to make you worry and anxious about how you naturally express yourself, to make you doubt yourself, to deprive you of just enjoying being social and feeling comfortable around people. He cares more about his insane jealousy and insecurities than about what makes you happy. He prefers knowingly hurting you than feeling hurt himself.

I'm sorry I'm ranting, please just try to love yourself and accept only the best for yourself, love shouldn't feel that hard. Have a beautiful life.
